mechanism: Adenosine receptor agonists for IOP lowering
note: Open-angle glaucoma / ocular hypertension; the A1 agonist trabodenoson is the only adenosine agonist with published patient data (Phase 2 signal 2016, Phase 3 MATRx-1 miss 2017 reported only by press release), while the A2A agonists OPA-6566 and evodenoson (ATL-313/DE-112) finished Phase 1/2 in 2012 with nothing posted or published.
label: Glaucoma (adenosine)

engagement.model: Normotensive cynomolgus monkey IOP / outflow facility
engagement.note: A1 agonist R-PIA raised monkey outflow facility 71%; no patient outflow-facility or target-engagement measurement published for trabodenoson or any A2A agonist.
engagement.quote: Total outflow facility was increased by 71% 3 hr after 100 micrograms R-PIA.
engagement.judgement: Myers 2016 (doi:10.1089/jop.2015.0148) infers an outflow mechanism from MMP-2 biology but measured only Goldmann IOP; Li 2018 (doi:10.1167/iovs.17-23212) measured facility in mice (+26-30%), not patients. Abstract plus full text read.

dose.note: Monkey dose-ranging (20-500 µg) set no exposure target; Phase 3 moved to 3-6% drops with no published animal bridge.
dose.quote: The effects of single or multiple topical doses of the relatively selective A1 adenosine receptor agonists (R)-phenylisopropyladenosine (R-PIA) and N6-cyclohexyladenosine (CHA) on intraocular pressure (IOP), aqueous humor flow (AHF) and outflow facility were investigated in ocular normotensive cynomolgus monkeys.
dose.judgement: Phase 2 (Myers 2016) saw no efficacy plateau up to 500 µg BID and Phase 3 (NCT02565173) ran 3.0%/6.0% QD and 4.5% BID; the only peer-reviewed account of the dose choice is a review (Qiu 2021, doi:10.1080/13543784.2021.1873276) blaming misread Phase 2 data, not an animal model. Li 2018 found 3% and 6% equipotent in mice (2.44 vs 2.45 mmHg) a year after the Phase 3 missed, with no comparison drawn.

efficacy.note: Topical A1 agonists lowered IOP 2-4 mmHg for 2-6 h in normotensive monkeys via outflow facility; rabbits agreed (Crosson 1995).
efficacy.quote: A single unilateral topical application of R-PIA (20-250 micrograms) or CHA (20-500 micrograms) produced ocular hypertension (maximum rise = 4.9 or 3.5 mmHg) within 30 min, followed by ocular hypotension (maximum fall = 2.1 or 3.6 mmHg) from 2-6 hr.

efficacy.model: Normotensive cynomolgus monkey IOP (class proxies R-PIA/CHA, not trabodenoson)
efficacy.note: Phase 2: trabodenoson 500 µg BID lowered IOP -4.1 vs -1.6 mmHg placebo in OHT/POAG patients, the direction animal models predicted.
efficacy.quote: Twice-daily ocular doses of trabodenoson, from 50 to 500 mcg, were well tolerated and showed a dose-related decrease in IOP that was statistically significant and clinically relevant at 500 mcg in patients with ocular hypertension or POAG.
efficacy.judgement: Myers's introduction states the animal-model prediction ('Selective A1 receptor agonism has been demonstrated to lower IOP in animal models while agonism of non-A1 receptors can elevate IOP') and the results confirm the direction in patients, so comparison_stated=true although no magnitude comparison is drawn; magnitude within_2x is my own juxtaposition (monkey fall 2.1-3.6 mmHg vs patient placebo-adjusted ~2.5 mmHg, raw 4.1). The 2017 Phase 3 MATRx-1 (NCT02565173, n=303, 12 weeks; no dose beat placebo at any of 12 time points; 6% QD -4.25 vs placebo -2.38 vs timolol -5.29 mmHg at 3 months per Inotek's January 2017 release and trade coverage) has no peer-reviewed report, no ClinicalTrials.gov results posting and no FDA review, so under evidence rule 1 it cannot carry a 'contra' entry; the only peer-reviewed discussion is a review (Qiu 2021, doi:10.1080/13543784.2021.1873276) that blames dose and regimen, not the model. Li 2018 (doi:10.1167/iovs.17-23212), a mouse paper, is the only primary source that itself asserts animal-human agreement ('Like CHA, trabodenoson effectively lowers IOP in several animal species, including humans') but it post-dates and ignores the Phase 3 miss. Trabodenoson's own monkey data exist only as ARVO abstracts, hence product_in_model=false.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey IOP (A2-mediated early rise); rabbit ocular blood flow
safety.note: Monkeys/rabbits flag A2-driven IOP rise and vasodilation for non-A1 agonists; Phase 2 trabodenoson hyperaemia (~19%) judged baseline imbalance; A2A patient data unpublished.
safety.short: A2 IOP rise flagged; hyperaemia unresolved
safety.quote: The relatively selective adenosine A2 antagonist 3,7-dimethyl-1-propargylxanthine (DMPX, 320 micrograms) inhibited the early hypertension, without influencing the hypotension.
safety.judgement: The hyperaemia story: A2 agonism raised IOP and broke the blood-aqueous barrier in rabbits/cats (Crosson 1996, PMID 8759351, no DOI) and dilated retinal vessels via A2A in rabbits (Konno 2007, doi:10.1016/j.lfs.2006.11.053), which is why trabodenoson was built A1-selective. In patients, Laties 2016 (healthy volunteers, doi:10.1089/jop.2015.0147) saw one hyperaemia case at the lowest dose; Myers 2016 reported conjunctival/ocular hyperaemia AEs in 16/85 (18.8%) trabodenoson subjects, 62.5% mild, and attributed them to a pre-dose imbalance (11.8% in the 500 µg group before drug) and single-site reporting bias. Neither paper compares with animal data, so not 'same'; no source attributes the hyperaemia to drug, so not 'contra'. The A2A agonists OPA-6566 (NCT01410188, Kubota Vision/Otsuka) and evodenoson/DE-112 (NCT01279083, Santen) completed Phase 1/2 in 2012 with no results posted and no publication, so the A2A hyperaemia prediction was never tested in print. Abstract-level for Konno and Crosson.
